svg.title: Layer 3 — Two-level clause matching strategy
svg.desc: L1 heading match handles simple cases. L2 semantic match catches restructured clauses. Both run always. Never skip L2.
svg.text: L1 + L2 ALWAYS run. Never skip L2. This catches restructured clauses.

g.text: The Problem: L1 Heading Match Alone
v1 Section 3 (Standstill) vs v2 Section 9.0 (Stand-Still) — SAME content, different numbers
L1 alone: REMOVED (v1 §3) + ADDED (v2 §9.0) — WRONG. Should be MODIFIED.
From L1+L2 combined: UNCHANGED | MODIFIED | ADDED | REMOVED
Key: if L1 found no match, L2 finds semantic match (same content, different structure)
Use difflib.ndiff() to show exact word changes
Never return "changed" without showing what changed

svg.text: 0.4–0.95 = MODIFIED (definitely same clause, but changed) → run word-level diff
< 0.4 = ADDED/REMOVED pair (too different, treat as separate)
Example: v1 §3 Standstill ↔ v2 §9.0 → ~0.75 cosine → MODIFIED ✓

g.text: v1: "Neither the Counterparty nor any affiliate... for a period..."
v2: "Each party agrees that, until one year... such party..."
Numbers: v1 §3, v2 §9.0 — L1 finds NO match
If this fails: L2 is broken. Test this first before moving to Layer 4.
